key_insight: Cova-PINN improves fluid-solid conjugate heat transfer predictions by enforcing conservation across coupled thermal paths, not just within separately sampled fluid and solid domains.
engineering_relevance: This makes PINNs more reliable for designing complex heat exchangers where accurate outlet temperature and end-to-end energy balance matter more than visually plausible temperature fields.
method: Cross-domain composite control-volume balances at the local scale
Paired-wall closure constraints at the global exchanger scale
Multi-domain PINN formulation for complex geometries and fluid-solid CHT
evidence_signal: On four TPMS heat exchangers, Cova-PINN cut average outlet-temperature error by 37.7% and device-level closure error by 60.2% versus the closest baseline, with consistent gains on a DualMS design.
watch_item: The approach adds more conservation constraints and paired-path bookkeeping, so performance may depend on accurate geometry partitioning and careful enforcement across interfaces.
paper_title: Cova-PINN: Cross-Domain Conservation Physics-Informed Neural Network for Fluid-Solid Conjugate Heat Transfer in Complex Geometries
